summary: Cuzco is a reworking of Java/Mask Trilogy where players place tiles to build a hex map of temples, houses, and terraces while bidding for turn order with a unique auction mechanism. It's a dense, elegant Kramer/Kiesling area-control and majority-scoring game where positioning and timing matter far more than luck.
praised: Clever turn-order auction where higher bids act later
High replayability due to map variability
Elegant production and layered rules that reward mastery
criticised: Steep learning curve and rules overhead for new players
Older-feeling design that some find fiddly compared to modern euros

interaction.detail: Players place tiles and structures onto one shared hex map, competing for area majority and zones of control on the same spaces. Taking a hex or building height there can block opponents from that location or majority, though there is no direct attacking of opponents' pieces.

subsystems: area-majority region scoring via terrain/building placement
scoring.how_you_win: You build terrain and place temples/houses to hold the most pieces in regions when they are triggered for scoring (repeatedly through the game and again at the end); the player with the most accumulated region-majority points wins.
